items.title: 68357_Jimmy Maxwell oral history interview
items.q: after my grandmother, Anne Reid, my mother's mother.

ctx.x: David, David Evans Maxwell. I gave him the middle name Evans after Gil Evans, who at that time was my best friend. Since then we've drifted apart quite a bit. But it's still a pretty name.

And my daughter was born three years after him and her name is Anne Reid Maxwell, after my grandmother, Anne Reid, my mother's mother. I don't know, in a burst of sentiment I did that. It was really unfair; I've thought about it over the years and I should have given her one of Gertrude's parents' names and one of my parents'. But in the Jewish religion, you don't name children after living people. And, see, we had to tell my mother-in-law that David was one of my relatives. David was just a name I liked from the…

The same thing came up when my son had his first son, he wanted to name him James Maxwell after me and his wife is Jewish and she wouldn't allow it. So he named him Justin, which is initial J, and gave him my father's first name, which is Kendrick, and it's also my middle name. Then recently he had another son, another baby, before she had it I said, "What are you going to name this one?" She said, "Well, if it's a girl, I'll name it James Maxwell." (Laughter.) So it was another boy.
